note: Commerce Stock Field defines the commerce_stock_level field type plus three widgets (commerce_stock_level_simple, commerce_stock_level_absolute, commerce_stock_level_simple_transaction) and a formatter (commerce_stock_level_simple). Attaching the field to a purchasable entity type (typically commerce_product_variation) lets editors view/adjust stock on the entity form; the widget creates a stock transaction via the stock service (so real storage needs commerce_stock_local). Medium/hard cases are grounded in real field + form-display config on the default product variation type, verified by pure config reads. All fixtures are namespaced field_csf_* and removed by cleanup (scoped, never a broad field purge).

evals.prompt: Which field type does the Commerce Stock Field module provide to let editors manage a product variation's stock, and what widgets can I choose for it?
evals.expected_output: The field type is commerce_stock_level. Its widgets are commerce_stock_level_simple, commerce_stock_level_absolute (enter the resulting level) and commerce_stock_level_simple_transaction (enter a signed adjustment); the formatter commerce_stock_level_simple shows the level read-only.

evals.prompt: How do I let editors edit stock on product variations using the Commerce Stock Field module, and what other submodule is required for the stock to actually be stored?
evals.expected_output: Create a commerce_stock_level field on the product variation type and pick one of its widgets on Manage form display. The widget writes a stock transaction via the stock service, so commerce_stock_local (the local_stock service) must be enabled and used by that variation type for stock to be stored.

evals.prompt: In the Commerce Stock Field module, which widget lets a warehouse user enter a signed stock adjustment (like +10 or -3) with a note, rather than typing the exact resulting quantity?
evals.expected_output: The commerce_stock_level_simple_transaction widget lets the user enter a signed transaction/adjustment (with an optional note), whereas commerce_stock_level_absolute expects the exact resulting level.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the default product variation type has a Commerce Stock level field (field_csf_stock). Inspect the live form display and state which stock widget it uses.
evals.expected_output: It uses the commerce_stock_level_absolute widget: core.entity_form_display.commerce_product_variation.default.default has content.field_csf_stock.type = commerce_stock_level_absolute.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the default product variation type has a field named field_csf_stock added by a Commerce Stock module. Inspect the live field storage and give its field type.
evals.expected_output: The field type is commerce_stock_level: field.storage.commerce_product_variation.field_csf_stock has type commerce_stock_level (the stock level field from commerce_stock_field).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, add a Commerce Stock level field with machine name field_csf_task to the default product variation type (commerce_product_variation, bundle default) so editors can manage stock on variations. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A field field_csf_task of type commerce_stock_level exists on commerce_product_variation bundle default (field.storage.commerce_product_variation.field_csf_task type = commerce_stock_level and the matching field.field config).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the default product variation type has a Commerce Stock level field field_csf_wtask currently using the simple stock widget. Change its form-display widget to the transaction widget (the one that records a signed stock adjustment). Apply the change to the live site.
